attractions.name: Long Point Trail
attractions.description: The trail crosses fields and forest before a steeper final approach to a rock outcrop overlooking the gorge and New River Gorge Bridge. The viewpoint has unprotected cliff edges.
attractions.evidence: Moderate; 1.6 miles/1.29 km (One-way); traverses field and forest; Long Point provides an outstanding overlook

conflicts.detail: The individual page pairs 1.6 miles with 1.29 km for a one-way distance; the units disagree.

attractions.name: Sandstone Falls Boardwalk
attractions.description: Bridges and boardwalks connect river islands and viewing decks beside Sandstone Falls. The route passes a riverside flatrock plant community associated with powerful Appalachian rivers.
attractions.accessibility: NPS describes the boardwalk as accessible; it crosses bridges to islands and observation decks.
attractions.evidence: Easy; Hiking and accessible; 0.2 miles/0.32 km (One-way); A 0.25 mile

conflicts.detail: The individual page gives 0.2 miles one way and describes 0.25 mile; no numeric length has been selected.

attractions.name: Brandywine Gorge Loop
attractions.description: From the falls trailhead, this loop descends into the gorge, crosses the creek on a footbridge, and returns by the falls viewing boardwalk. A lower viewing deck requires additional steps.
attractions.accessibility: The gorge loop is not wheelchair accessible: its unpaved surface is hilly and rocky in places. A separate short path reaches the upper boardwalk viewing area for wheelchair users.
attractions.evidence: This trail is not wheelchair accessible.; geology

conflicts.detail: The activity page gives 1.5 miles round trip; the park hiking table lists 1.4 miles.

attractions.name: Ledges Trail
attractions.description: The trail follows the Ledges rock formations and connects with other routes in the Virginia Kendall area. An overlook and the exposed Sharon Conglomerate are features of this landscape.
attractions.accessibility: NPS states that the trail is not accessible to visitors with mobility impairments.
attractions.evidence: The trail is not accessible to visitors with mobility impairments.; creation out of Sharon Conglomerate

conflicts.detail: The dedicated page describes 1.8 miles around the formations; the hiking table lists 2.2 miles, with unresolved route scope.

attractions.name: Riverside Walk
attractions.description: A paved path follows the Virgin River from the Temple of Sinawava into narrowing sandstone walls. It reaches the beginning of The Narrows; entering the river is a separate continuation.
attractions.accessibility: Paving is irregular in places, minor drop-offs occur, and sand can make the concrete slippery. NPS reports steep sections; paving alone does not establish wheelchair suitability for the whole route.
attractions.evidence: paving is irregular in some sections and minor drop-offs are present; canyon carving, erosion

conflicts.detail: The accessibility survey gives 1 mile one way; the spring 2026 guide gives 2.2 miles round trip.

attractions.name: Pa'rus Trail
attractions.description: The main trail connects Zion Canyon Visitor Center with Canyon Junction along the Virgin River, offering Watchman views and interpretive exhibits. It is shared with bicycles and leashed pets.
attractions.accessibility: NPS describes the main route as wheelchair accessible. The optional unpaved connector to the Human History Museum is not designed for wheelchairs.
attractions.evidence: It is accessible for wheelchairs, pets on leashes, and bicycles.; geology

conflicts.detail: The individual page describes 3.5 miles end-to-end and 1.6 miles one way in its survey; the spring 2026 guide labels 3.5 miles round trip.
